html:
The Wapishana are an Arawak-speaking people of the Rupununi savannas of south-west Guyana and the neighbouring part of Roraima state in Brazil. They live in villages, grow cassava, hunt and fish in the grasslands and forest edges, and are known for basketry and cassava graters.

Their land sat on the disputed border between British and Portuguese, later Brazilian, claims. An arbitration of 1904 fixed the line and split the Wapishana between British Guiana and Brazil. Their neighbours are the Carib-speaking Macushi, and many villages are now mixed. In Brazil some live in the Raposa Serra do Sol reserve, upheld by the supreme court in 2009.
